papers.title: Detecting and Preventing Data Poisoning Attacks on AI Models
papers.abstract: This paper investigates the critical issue of data poisoning attacks on AI models, a growing concern in the ever-evolving landscape of artificial intelligence and cybersecurity. As advanced technology systems become increasingly prevalent across various sectors, the need for robust defence mechanisms against adversarial attacks becomes paramount. The study aims to develop and evaluate novel techniques for detecting and preventing data poisoning attacks, focusing on both theoretical frameworks and practical applications. Through a comprehensive literature review, experimental validation using the CIFAR-10 and Insurance Claims datasets, and the development of innovative algorithms, this paper seeks to enhance the resilience of AI models against malicious data manipulation. The study explores various methods, including anomaly detection, robust optimization strategies, and ensemble learning, to identify and mitigate the effects of poisoned data during model training. Experimental results indicate that data poisoning significantly degrades model performance, reducing classification accuracy by up to 27 % in image recognition tasks (CIFAR-10) and 22 % in fraud detection models (Insurance Claims dataset). The proposed defence mechanisms, including statistical anomaly detection and adversarial training, successfully mitigated poisoning effects, improving model robustness and restoring accuracy levels by an average of $15-20 \%$. The findings further demonstrate that ensemble learning techniques provide an additional layer of resilience, reducing false positives and false negatives caused by adversarial data injections. The findings of this paper contribute to the broader understanding of adversarial machine learning and provide actionable insights for practitioners in industries facing emerging threats to AI-based systems. By addressing the challenges of data poisoning attacks, this study aims to improve the security and reliability of AI models, ultimately fostering greater trust in AI technologies across critical applications.

papers.title: Robust and Adaptive Dual-Defense Framework Against Data Poisoning Attacks in Recommendation Systems
papers.abstract: Deep learning-based recommendation systems are highly vulnerable to data poisoning attacks, where adversaries manipulate user interactions to degrade model integrity. We hypothesize that combining an active robust loss with a passive GAN-based detection will significantly reduce poisoning impact in recommendation systems without sacrificing utility. We propose a robust and adaptive dual-defense framework: the active defense integrates a crafted loss function to mitigate poisoning effects while maintaining model performance. The passive defense employs a Generative Adversarial Network (GAN)-based detection model to identify and filter poisoned data, enhancing detection accuracy and system security. The framework supports classical matrix factorization (MF) model and large language model (LLM)-based pipelines and scales to large datasets. Extensive experiments across multiple real-world datasets at varying poison rates show that our method outperforms representative defenses, consistently reducing attack success without sacrificing recommendation quality. The framework also admits a federated instantiation, where robust training and GAN-based detection run on clients and only privacy-preserving summaries are aggregated. The proposed method significantly improves the robustness and adaptability of recommendation systems under data poisoning attacks.

papers.title: Adaptive AI-Driven Learning Architecture for Real Time Detection and Prevention of Data Poisoning and Model Evasion Attacks
papers.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) has been integrated into cybersecurity systems particularly in cyber threat intelligence (CTI) and has significantly enhanced the detection, analysis, and mitigation of sophisticated cyber threats in real time in organisations. Unlike traditional static defence mechanisms, which rely on fixed rules or offline retraining, the proposed architecture empowers continuous dynamic learning capabilities to identify and mitigate attacks as they unfold ensuring the integrity and reliability of AI-driven CTI systems. AI models to self-heal and harden against evolving adversarial tactics. The primary goal is to enhance CTI operations by providing timely, accurate threat detection and robust mitigation thereby reducing the window of opportunity for attackers and improving overall cybersecurity posture. This article presents a comprehensive adaptive learning architecture with formalised threat models, architectural specifications, and empirical validation. Experimental evaluation using benchmark datasets (CIC-IDS2017 and VirusTotal) demonstrates that the system achieves 43.7% higher evasion detection accuracy than traditional static anomaly detectors, while maintaining processing latency below 5 milliseconds. The architecture successfully detects 89.1% of poisoning attacks and reduces false positive rates by 37.5% relative to baseline methods. The key contributions of this article include the design of an integrated adaptive learning system that simultaneously detects and prevents both data poisoning and model evasion attacks within cybersecurity AI models.

papers.title: Resilient Autonomy: Securing Intelligent Systems Against Adversarial Attacks
papers.abstract: As autonomous systems become central to mission-critical operations, their ability to withstand adversarial threats is crucial to ensuring trust, safety, and uninterrupted functionality. This paper introduces a comprehensive framework for resilient autonomy that proactively prevents, detects, and mitigates key adversarial challenges, including sensor spoofing, sensor manipulation, and machine learning model poisoning. We present a layered defense architecture that integrates adversarial robust learning, real-time anomaly detection, and secure control strategies to maintain reliable autonomous behavior in compromised environments. Our hybrid resilience model addresses both inference-time perturbations and upstream vulnerabilities in data acquisition and processing pipelines. The system employs adaptive decision logic and decentralized failover mechanisms to dynamically reconfigure operations upon detection of anomalies or suspicious behavior, thus preserving mission continuity. In addition, we embed explainable AI modules to enhance transparency, facilitate system diagnostics, and support operator trust. We validate the proposed framework using a suite of simulated adversarial scenarios across diverse autonomous agents, including drones, mobile robots, and vehicle models. Results demonstrate significant gains in threat resistance, operational stability, and recovery time when compared to conventional defenses. This work lays the foundation for building self-reliant, attack-aware autonomous systems that are capable of sustaining functionality under adversarial uncertainty.

summary: The literature on robust AI systems against data poisoning and adversarial attacks reveals three primary themes: the development of defense mechanisms for data poisoning, the enhancement of robustness in machine learning against adversarial attacks, and the resilience of autonomous systems. Key findings highlight innovative frameworks such as dual-defense architectures and adaptive learning systems, yet limitations include a focus on specific datasets and a lack of empirical validation in real-world scenarios. Notably, gaps remain in the adaptability of these defenses across diverse applications and the need for comprehensive studies on adversarial training methods, emphasizing the importance of operationalizing constructs for practical implementations.
scholarly_positioning: While existing literature has made significant strides in developing defense mechanisms against data poisoning and adversarial attacks, such as dual-defense frameworks and robust adversarial training, these approaches often remain confined to specific datasets and lack empirical validation in diverse real-world contexts. The reliance on theoretical frameworks and simulated scenarios raises concerns about the adaptability and effectiveness of these defenses against evolving attack strategies. Furthermore, there is a notable gap in the integration of explainable AI and adaptive learning architectures that can dynamically respond to adversarial threats. This proposed research aims to bridge these gaps by operationalizing constructs that enhance resilience across various AI applications, thereby contributing to a more robust understanding of AI system security in practical environments.
research_scope: This study will focus on enhancing the resilience of recommendation systems against data poisoning attacks through the implementation of a robust dual-defense framework. The target population will consist of various recommendation algorithms deployed in e-commerce platforms, evaluated over a six-month period. The intervention will involve the integration of an active robust loss mechanism and a GAN-based detection system, compared against a baseline of traditional recommendation algorithms without these defenses. Primary outcomes will include the reduction in attack success rates and the maintenance of recommendation quality, while secondary outcomes will assess the adaptability of the defense mechanisms across different datasets and evolving attack strategies. This empirical study aims to provide insights into the practical applicability and effectiveness of advanced defense strategies in real-world scenarios.
concept_definition:
{
  "Robust AI Systems": "AI systems designed to maintain performance and reliability in the presence of adversarial conditions, such as data poisoning and attacks.",
  "Data Poisoning": "A type of attack where malicious data is injected into the training dataset to manipulate the learning process of the model.",
  "Adversarial Attacks": "Techniques used to deceive machine learning models by providing misleading inputs that cause incorrect outputs.",
  "Recommendation Systems": "Algorithms that predict user preferences and suggest products or content based on historical data.",
  "Dual-Defense Framework": "A defense strategy that combines two distinct mechanisms to enhance the resilience of a system against attacks.",
  "Active Robust Loss Mechanism": "A loss function designed to minimize the impact of adversarial examples during model training, ensuring that the model remains robust.",
  "GAN-based Detection System": "A Generative Adversarial Network used to identify and filter out poisoned data from the training set.",
  "Empirical Validation": "The process of testing hypotheses through real-world data and experiments to assess the effectiveness of proposed methods.",
  "Ablation Studies": "Experiments that systematically remove or alter components of a system to understand their contributions to overall performance.",
  "Evaluation Metrics": "Quantitative measures used to assess the effectiveness of the defense mechanisms, such as attack success rates and recommendation quality.",
  "Adaptability": "The ability of a defense mechanism to maintain effectiveness across different datasets and evolving attack strategies.",
  "Resilience": "The capacity of a system to continue functioning effectively in the face of adversarial challenges."
}

Additionally, if internal representations of the models are to be analyzed, access to open-source models or hidden-state extraction will be necessary. Since the study involves empirical validation and comparisons between different algorithms, it may also benefit from a clear annotation protocol for the datasets used. No human participants are required, and ethics approval is not necessary. A feasible adjustment would be to ensure access to suitable labeled datasets and GPU resources before proceeding with the study.
gap: Prior studies have demonstrated the effectiveness of dual-defense frameworks against data poisoning attacks in recommendation systems; however, they treat the adaptability of these frameworks across diverse AI applications as fixed, leaving unclear whether the integration of active robust loss and GAN-based detection affects the resilience of other machine learning models. This matters practically because the evolving nature of adversarial threats necessitates adaptable defenses that can operate effectively in various contexts; therefore, this study investigates the applicability of the proposed dual-defense framework across different recommendation algorithms and datasets.
question: How does the integration of an active robust loss mechanism and a GAN-based detection system within a dual-defense framework affect the resilience and recommendation quality of various recommendation algorithms against data poisoning attacks in e-commerce platforms?
theoretical_mechanism: The proposed research investigates the integration of an active robust loss mechanism (independent variable) and a GAN-based detection system (mediator) within a dual-defense framework to enhance the resilience (dependent variable) of various recommendation algorithms against data poisoning attacks. The theoretical framework is grounded in adversarial machine learning, which posits that the effectiveness of defense mechanisms can be improved through adaptive learning strategies. The causal chain suggests that the active robust loss mechanism minimizes the impact of adversarial examples, while the GAN-based detection system filters out poisoned data, thereby improving system-level outcomes such as attack success rates and recommendation quality. User-level outcomes, such as user satisfaction, are expected to be influenced by perceived transparency of the recommendation process, which is mediated by the effectiveness of the dual-defense framework. Assumptions requiring empirical validation include the adaptability of the defense mechanisms across different datasets and the direct impact of defense effectiveness on user satisfaction.
hypothesis: The integration of an active robust loss mechanism and a GAN-based detection system within a dual-defense framework will significantly reduce the attack success rates (primary dependent variable) of various recommendation algorithms compared to traditional algorithms without these defenses, thereby enhancing the resilience of the systems against data poisoning attacks.

The study will utilize a diverse set of real-world datasets from e-commerce platforms to train and evaluate the recommendation systems over a six-month period. A baseline group will consist of traditional recommendation algorithms without the dual-defense mechanisms, allowing for comparative analysis. Key operationalized variables include attack success rates and recommendation quality, measured through simulation results and user feedback, respectively. Evaluation metrics will include statistical significance tests to validate the effectiveness of the defenses, while potential confounds such as dataset characteristics will be controlled through stratified sampling. The study aims for reproducibility by documenting model configurations and evaluation protocols, ensuring that findings can be independently verified.

proposal: This research proposal aims to enhance the resilience of recommendation systems against data poisoning attacks by implementing a dual-defense framework that integrates an active robust loss mechanism and a GAN-based detection system. The study will focus on various recommendation algorithms deployed in e-commerce platforms, utilizing real-world datasets over a six-month period. Key concepts include Robust AI Systems, Data Poisoning, Adversarial Attacks, and the Dual-Defense Framework, defined operationally to ensure clarity. The study assumes access to labeled datasets and GPU resources for model training, with a contingency plan for dataset acquisition. Despite significant advancements in defense mechanisms, existing literature reveals a gap in empirical validation across diverse applications, particularly regarding the adaptability of these frameworks to different recommendation algorithms and datasets. The central research question investigates how the integration of the proposed mechanisms affects resilience and recommendation quality, specifically examining the interplay between the active robust loss mechanism (independent variable) and the GAN-based detection system (mediator) on attack success rates (dependent variable) and user satisfaction (user-level outcome). The hypothesis posits that the dual-defense framework will significantly reduce attack success rates compared to traditional algorithms without these defenses. Construct operationalization will include metrics for attack success rates, recommendation quality, and user satisfaction, measured through simulation results and user feedback. The methodology will involve comparative analysis against traditional algorithms, controlling for dataset characteristics and employing statistical tests for validity. Expected contributions include theoretical advancements in dual-defense frameworks, development of robust evaluation metrics, and empirical findings validating the framework's effectiveness in real-world scenarios. Novelty lies in the integration of adaptive learning strategies within the proposed framework, while limitations include potential confounds related to dataset diversity and the inability to generalize findings across all AI applications.
